key_idea: A learned differentiable transformation network imitates how a photo-realistic renderer changes a textured object, so adversarial vehicle camouflage can be optimised with CARLA-level realism and tested on a scaled real car.
method: The network learns the expected transformation of a rendered object when its texture changes; the attack is optimised through it; evaluation in CARLA on Unreal Engine and on a scaled Tesla Model 3.
data: CARLA (Unreal Engine); scaled Tesla Model 3 demonstration (abstract).
reported_result: Abstract: camouflaged 3D vehicles evade state-of-the-art detectors in CARLA, and the scaled-car demonstration shows transfer to the real world; no numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Questions 2 and 3: a simulator-in-the-loop route from rendering to physical tests; the learned transformation is the same kind of bridge as P2-P1802. Whole-body vehicle camouflage, so slide 01 patch-region cues do not apply directly.
notes: Crossref (CVPR 2022) and arXiv API (2022) records match. Also catalogued metadata-only as P2-P2317 (LIT_X14).
